name: Abu Tammam
bio: Habib ibn Aws al-Ta'i was born in Jasim, a village of the Hawran in Syria, in 188 AH (804 CE), and travelled to Egypt before the caliph al-Mu'tasim summoned him to Baghdad, rewarded him and set him above the poets of his day. Al-Zirikli calls him “one of the princes of eloquence” and his verse strong and weighty; opinion has long been divided over whether he, al-Mutanabbi or al-Buhturi was the greater poet. He knew by heart, al-Zirikli says, fourteen thousand rajaz poems of the Arabs besides the odes and short pieces, and he compiled the Hamasa, an anthology of the older poets. He was made master of the post at Mosul and died there before he had held it two years, in 231 AH (846 CE).
